paragraphs.notes: Continuation of Tabelle 4, 'Bindungslaengen [A] und Bindungswinkel der Kristallmodifikation II', whose caption is printed on page 5 and NOT on this page. This page prints only the bare word '(fortgesetzt)' above the table. Evidence for the identification: page 5 carries the Tabelle 4 caption and the first part of this same table, its last printed row is O(3B)-C(9B)-C(10B) 112.3(3), and this page opens with C(8)-O(3B) 1.495(3); the A/B disorder labels (C(9A)/C(9B), C(10A)/C(10B), F(1A)/F(1B) and so on) occur in Tabelle 4 and nowhere in Tabelle 3, which uses undecorated C(9), C(10), F(1). COLUMN STRUCTURE: four ruled columns, headed 'Bindung | A(deg) | Bindung | A(deg)'. That is one label/value pair repeated twice side by side to save vertical space, NOT four independent data series; the two halves are read as two separate continuations of the same single list, left pair first, then right pair. The left pair carries 34 rows and the right pair 21, so the right pair runs out level with the left pair's row 21 (C(2)-C(3)-Cl(1)) and the last 13 rows of the left pair stand alone with the right half of the rule blank. Those blank cells are printed blank; they are not unreadable. UNITS: the shared heading 'A(deg)' carries both units at once and which one applies is decided by the LABEL, not by the column. A two-atom label such as C(8)-O(3B) is a bond LENGTH in Angstrom; a three-atom label such as F(3B)-C(10B)-F(1B) is a bond ANGLE in degrees. On this page the first 7 rows of the left pair are lengths and every remaining row of both pairs is an angle. BRACKETED NUMBER: in 1.495(3) the (3) is the estimated standard uncertainty on the last quoted digit, in units of that last digit. It is not a footnote reference and not a count of anything. Transcribed exactly as printed, including 1.267(16), where the uncertainty runs to two digits. A/B DISORDER SUFFIXES: this page carries atom labels with a trailing A or B, O(3A), O(3B), C(9A), C(9B), C(10A), C(10B), F(1A), F(1B), F(2A), F(2B), F(3A), F(3B). These are disorder components, two alternative refined positions for the same atom at partial occupancy. Every suffix is transcribed exactly; dropping the A/B would merge two distinct refined positions into one. The row O(3A)-C(8)-O(3B) 30.21(15) is the angle BETWEEN the two alternative oxygen positions at C(8), which is why it is only about 30 degrees; it is printed as shown and is not a transcription error. AS PRINTED: the value in row C(3)-C(2)-C(1) is set as '116.11 (14)', with a space before the bracket, unlike every other value on the page. The page image and the text layer agree on the space, so it is kept. The same typesetting slip occurs on page 5 (116.81 (16), 120.1 (2)). The table has no [00NN] marker of its own and none is printed on this page; following the shared briefing it is attached to the nearest preceding numbered paragraph, which is [0018] on page 3. The prose of [0018] itself lives on page 3 and is not repeated here. Only the rows printed on this page are recorded; page 5 carries the earlier rows and they are not repeated. Decimal points are printed as points, not German commas, throughout both tables on this page.

Tabelle 5, caption printed in full on this page directly above the table. COLUMN STRUCTURE: four ruled columns of bare numbers with NO column headings; the unit is carried once, in the caption, as [2θ], so all 46 values are diffraction angles in degrees 2 theta. The four columns are one single ascending list broken into four columns to fit the page, read DOWN column 1 (7.3765 to 19.3008), then down column 2 (20.8117 to 25.7119), then column 3 (26.6207 to 31.2971), then column 4 (32.4069 to 36.7974). Read across the rows instead and the list is not monotonic, which is the check that the column reading is the right one. Columns 1 to 3 hold 12 values each and column 4 holds 10, so the bottom two cells of column 4 are printed blank. CONTINUATION: this table is continued on page 7 under '(fortgesetzt)', where a 13th row of the same four-column grid prints 20.4034, 25.9248 and 31.6675 with the fourth cell blank. Column-wise those three append to the foot of columns 1, 2 and 3 respectively, and only that reading keeps the full list ascending (19.3008, 20.4034, 20.8117 ...), which independently confirms the column reading. Those three values are printed on page 7 and are deliberately not recorded here. Counting only what this page prints, columns 1 to 3 hold 12 values and column 4 holds 10. No standard uncertainties are given in this table; every value is a plain four-decimal number. Like the block above it, the table has no [00NN] marker of its own, so it is attached to [0018], the nearest preceding numbered paragraph, which is printed on page 3.

notes: The page carries no prose sentence at all, no [00NN] marker, no section heading and no chemical structure: it is two tables, the header 'EP 2 045 236 A1', the page number 6 in the footer, and the EPO margin line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 printed down the left edge. The margin numbers are typesetting furniture, not content, and are not recorded as data. 'drawings' is empty and that is a finding, not an omission: there is no drawn structure and no spectrum on this page. 'discrepancies' is empty because there is no prose on this page to check the tables against. page_confidence is high: the page is born digital, the text layer at /tmp/ep2045/page06.txt agrees digit for digit with the page image for every one of the 55 bond rows and 46 diffraction values, and the only thing the text layer could not supply, the column structure, was read off the image. The extractor happened to walk this page row-major with all four cells present per row, so its flat run does preserve the pairing here; that was confirmed against the image rather than assumed.
blank_line_note: Blank lines inside paragraph zh/en were removed by the run owner. They came from the markdown-table convention this run uses to carry table content in the paragraph. build_enriched.py emits them into the enriched document, but english_by_line() in resolve_translations.py builds its `body` with `if t.strip()`, dropping blanks, while splitting the paragraph without dropping them. Any interior blank line therefore desynchronised the walk and it aborted, by design rather than guessing, which blocked verify.py for the whole run. Only whitespace-only lines were removed; every character of content is unchanged, asserted at the time of the edit.
